articleTitle: High-Power Microwave Damage Protection Design of GaN HEMT by Gate Structure Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: GaN HEMT devices have promising applications in the field of RF front-end technology but are often susceptible to electromagnetic interference from the environment or targeted by attacks from electromagnetic weapons. This paper proposes a design methodology based on gate structure optimization, introducing three types of GaN HEMT gate structures: I-shaped, T-shaped, and V-shaped gates. The electrothermal responses of these devices under high-power microwave injection at varying amplitudes were simulated and analyzed. The results indicate that the heat generation mechanisms and temperature distributions differ among the devices, with the V-shaped gate device exhibiting the longest burnout time. This study provides insights for the reliability design and electromagnetic protection of GaN HEMT devices.

articleTitle: An Automated Data Mining Framework Using Autoencoders for Feature Extraction and Dimensionality Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This study proposes an automated data mining framework based on autoencoders and experimentally verifies its effectiveness in feature extraction and data dimensionality reduction. Through the encoding-decoding structure, the autoencoder can capture the data's potential characteristics and achieve noise reduction and anomaly detection, providing an efficient and stable solution for the data mining process. The experiment compared the performance of the autoencoder with traditional dimensionality reduction methods (such as PCA, FA, T-SNE, and UMAP). The results showed that the autoencoder performed best in terms of reconstruction error and root mean square error and could better retain data structure and enhance the generalization ability of the model. The autoencoder-based framework not only reduces manual intervention but also significantly improves the automation of data processing. In the future, with the advancement of deep learning and big data technology, the autoencoder method combined with a generative adversarial network (GAN) or graph neural network (GNN) is expected to be more widely used in the fields of complex data processing, real-time data analysis and intelligent decision-making.

articleTitle: Specific Emitter Identification Based on Wavelet Convolution Supervised Contrast Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Specific emitter identification technology has an important role in military and civilian fields, and it is a new idea to apply contrast learning in the field of specific emitter identification. The traditional supervised contrast learning algorithm has the problem of low recognition accuracy, so we propose a wavelet convolution supervised contrast learning ( Wavelet Convolution Supervised Contrast Learning, WC-SupCon) algorithm for specific emitter identification. Firstly, the bispectral maps of I/Q signals are generated; then, they are inputted into the feature extraction layer of WC-ResNet (Wavelet Convolution ResNet), and the parameters of the feature extraction network are updated and trained by the supervised contrast loss function; finally, the parameter weights of the feature extraction network are kept constant, and the cross-entropy loss function is used to train the classification network, which can complete the task of specific emitter identification. specific emitter identification task. The experimental results show that the accuracy of specific emitter identification based on wavelet convolution supervised contrast learning is 92.47%, which is 12.59% higher than that of the traditional network. Therefore, the method proposed in this paper has more practical value for contrast learning in the field of specific emitter identification.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Software Reuse Identification Method Based on Code Similarity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Software reuse techniques have become a pervasive research hotspot in today's software engineering field. The most researched and widely applied is combinatorial technology, which is software reuse technology based on artifacts. The construction and identification of artifacts is a hot issue in this field, and the paper presents a software artifact identification method based on program code similarity analysis. The technical application is carried out.

articleTitle: Multi-head Discretization improves Learning Ability in Vector Quantization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: The quantization mechanism introduced in the Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE) model is equivalent to defining a potential quantization codebook for the model, the size of which affects the overall performance of VQ-VAE. In this paper, we design a multi-head discrete quantization mechanism from the perspective of Vector Quantization (VQ). The mechanism learns further data features by refining the processing of the data in the VQ process, which aims to improve the ability of the VQ model to learn the data and increase the utilization of the codebook, and its performance evaluation index is the Mean Squared Error (MSE) between the reconstructed images and the original images of the model. Our experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate the feasibility of the multi-head discrete quantization mechanism, and prove that increasing the number of heads appropriately is beneficial to the reconstruction performance of the model.

articleTitle: Direct Torque Control of Low-Pulsation Dual Three-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Using Master-Slave Voltage Vector
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In the traditional direct torque control process of dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motors, there are relatively large current harmonics as well as flux and torque fluctuations. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a new low-pulsation direct torque control strategy for dual three-phase motors based on the duty cycle distribution of master-slave virtual vectors. Firstly, this strategy adopts the direct torque control strategy of virtual vector synthesis to achieve the suppression of harmonic currents. Next, the voltage vectors of the dual three-phase motor are divided into master control virtual vectors and slave virtual vectors. The duty cycles of the master-slave virtual vectors are recalculated and distributed according to the evaluation function. In one cycle, there is the joint action of the master-slave virtual vectors and zero vectors to achieve the precise control of torque and flux. The results show that the proposed strategy effectively reduces the torque and flux pulsations and suppresses the harmonic currents.

articleTitle: Symbol Synchronization Algorithm Based on Delay Multiplication for Non-cooperative Communication Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In order to monitor non-cooperative communication signals, a symbol synchronization algorithm for non-cooperative signals is proposed based on delay multiplication. We estimate a rough value of the symbol rate by estimating the bandwidth of non-cooperative signals. Determining the delay time with the rough symbol rate, we obtain the Fourier component of the symbol rate by delay multiplication. Then we estimate the symbol rate accurately by spectral line detection and extract the symbol synchronization clock by filtering and shaping. The proposed algorithm can be calculated quickly by FFT and is robust, which is useful in monitoring of non-cooperative signals. Simulation results show that the algorithm can estimate symbol rate and extract symbol synchronization clock accurately when the SNR is greater than -4.5 dB. Experiment results of cooperative signal show that the algorithm can estimate the symbol rate with high accuracy and obtain the symbol synchronization clock accurately. Experiment results of non-cooperative signals show that the algorithm is also effective for non-cooperative signals.

articleTitle: Cryo-CMOS Model-Enabled 8-bit 32 MS/s SAR ADC with Split Capacitor Array
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This article presents a cryogenic 8-bit successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) using Nexchip 110 nm 1P6M CMOS technology for the readout of qubits. To mitigate the base freeze-out effect of bipolar junction transistors at cryogenic temperature and the resulting unavailable BJT-based bandgap voltage reference circuits, a VCM -based switching procedure through a capacitive DAC with top-plate sampling split capacitor array was employed. By the adoption of compact cryo-CMOS SPICE model and asynchronous control logic, the ADC achieves an SNDR of 41.56 dB and consumes 2.1 mW while maintaining the Walden FoM of 646 fJ/conv.-step at 4.2 K and 32 MS/s. The converter occupies an active area of 0.106 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Location Protection Mechanism in Sparse Mobile CrowdSensing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: As Internet of Things technology advances quickly, Sparse Mobile CrowdSensing has been used as a productive way to collect and process data. Leveraging the real time capabilities and wide coverage of Internet of Things communication, Sparse Mobile CrowdSensing utilizes distributed sensing nodes to collect and process real-time data, thereby supporting diverse intelligent services. In practical scenarios, users are often required to upload data carrying location information to support subsequent data completion. However, such data can expose sensitive user information, posing significant privacy risks. To mitigate these risks, location obfuscation techniques are employed to reduce the likelihood of privacy leakage. Nevertheless, these privacy-preserving measures can significantly degrade the quality of data completion. To address this challenge, we propose a scheme that integrates data correction to balance privacy protection and data completion quality. Specifically, our approach obfuscates location data using geographic indistinguishability and leverages historical data to obtain the data regularity, enabling modifications to the obfuscated data to ensure its usability. Our mechanism performs better than other baseline methods in terms of ensuring data completion accuracy while preserving a certain degree of privacy, according to evaluation on the real datasets.

articleTitle: Image dehazing method based on visual state space model and depth information assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Image dehazing, as a low-level visual task, has always been a challenging research topic in computer vision. This paper proposes a dehazing algorithm, UDMDN, based on the visual state space model and augmented with depth information. First, a mamba dehazing network based on U-net is proposed, which has efficient modelling capabilities while reducing computational consumption; second, a gating mechanism and a deep separable convolutional feedforward network are introduced to achieve better feature extraction capabilities; finally, the dehazing network and the depth estimation network are collaborated to use differential information to better guide the dehazing network to focus on the foggy area, and the dehazing effect is further improved by uncertainty loss optimization. Experimental results show that the model proposed in this paper has better dehazing performance than existing models.

articleTitle: ADP: An Adaptive Downgrade Predictor for Hybrid Multi-Die Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Downgrade prediction technique speculatively writes dirty data back from cache to memory by predicting the last-touch or last-write-touch of a cache block, allowing subsequent memory access requests from other cores to directly read data from the LLC or memory, hiding the additional delay caused by coherence activities. Previous downgrade prediction techniques, namely LDP, which typically employ a PAp approach to maintain prediction coverage, suffers from low coverage when the program does not exhibit enough repeated patterns within a block address. A way to address this issue is to employ a PAg approach, which is called GDP in this paper, to allow sharing of a same signature across different other block addresses, with the disadvantage of higher misprediction ratio. This paper proposes an Adaptive Downgrade Predictor, ADP, which makes us of a Choice Predictor, to select the best predictor for a given block address at the runtime to achieve high coverage in GDP while maintaining low misprediction like LDP for each application. The experimental results show that the average prediction coverage of LDP and GDP are 79% and 72.5% respectively, with the average misprediction rate of are 1.8% and 10.2% respectively. With ADP, the average prediction coverage is 86.3%, increased by 7.3% as compared to LDP and by 13.8% as compared to GDP, with the average misprediction rate of 3.3%, significantly decreased by 6.9% as compared to GDP but slightly increased by 1.5% as compared to LDP.

articleTitle: A Tensor-Based Underdetermined Blind Identification Algorithm of Compound Radar Jamming Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In order to convert compound radar jamming signals into individual jamming signals, while improving the accuracy of blind identification, this paper presents a novel underdetermined blind identification approach resorting to tensor decomposition. First, the autocovariance matrices for each individual sub-block are determined and subsequently stacked to form the third-order symmetric tensor of observed signals. Then, an optimal step proximal alternating least squares (OS-PALS) method with a self-adaptive step size selection rule is proposed to decompose the constructed tensor, which guarantees the convergence and accelerates the convergence rate in tensor decomposition. Finally, singular value decomposition (SVD) is used to eliminate the influence of error factors. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach surpasses existing methods in regard to blind identification performance in common application scenarios.

articleTitle: Student Performance Prediction Using Stacking Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Student grade prediction is an important research topic in educational data mining. To address the issues of low prediction accuracy and poor generalization encountered by single models in predicting student grades, this paper proposes a Stacking ensemble learning model that integrates multiple individual models. The proposed model uses Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree, and Random Forest as base learners, with Logistic Regression (LR) serving as the metalearner, forming a two-layer Stacking ensemble learning framework. The results demonstrate that the Stacking ensemble learning model achieves an accuracy of 91.6%, precision of 92.1%, recall of 93.8%, and an F1-score of 93.0%. These performance metrics are significantly better than those of individual learning models, indicating that the proposed Stacking model can effectively predict students' academic performance.

articleTitle: Research on an Improved Weighted Average Passive Localization Algorithm in Spherical Coordinates
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This paper addresses the direction-finding problem in passive localization systems and proposes a novel algorithm for direction finding passive localization using an improved weighted average method in spherical coordinates. By constructing a suitable mathematical model and utilizing a weighted average algorithm for estimating the direction of received signals, the precision and reliability of localization are significantly enhanced. Experimental results demonstrate that this algorithm maintains higher stability and accuracy under conditions of large errors compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Assisted Readout of In Situ Frequency Tunable Superconducting Qubits
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Dispersive readout of superconducting qubits is one of the most critical components of superconducting quantum computing systems. Traditional dispersive readout schemes typically employ digital signal processing technique to demodulate multiple measurements into clouds in the IQ plane, determining the qubit state through projection and threshold analysis. However, when addressing tunable qubits, this method is limited to single-frequency measurements; attempting to measure at different frequencies without adjusting the readout frequency accordingly can compromise readout fidelity. To address this, this paper proposes a deep learning-based readout scheme that can directly train and predict the readout signals corresponding to the ground and excited states of the same superconducting qubit at different frequencies under a fixed readout frequency. A supervised learning approach is utilized to construct a deep learning model based on the multilayer perceptron. The trained model can directly predict the qubit state at different frequencies within a large frequency range. Moreover, the deep learning model can not only distinguish between the ground and excited states of the qubit but also leverage its capability to handle regression problems to test any superposition state of the qubit, which has been verified through Rabi oscillation tests. Experimental results indicate that this approach can effectively discern the state within a 300 MHz tuning range of the qubit frequency, achieving a readout fidelity exceeding 92% under various magnetic flux bias and a Rabi measurement fidelity above 96%. The findings of this study underscore the efficacy of the deep learning scheme in augmenting the convenience of qubit readout processes, concurrently preserving high fidelity, which is imperative for the advancement of quantum computing technologies.

articleTitle: Research on S-band Receiver Design for Wireless Data Link Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: The S-band receiver plays an important role in radio data link systems. In this paper, a S-band receiver is designed according to the requirements of wireless data reception link. The receiving front end uses a bandpass filtering scheme, and the intermediate frequency after downconversion uses a low-pass filtering scheme. Through the design and link optimization simulation of the receiver, the test results show that the working frequency is (2.7~3.2) GHz, the gain is better than 30dB, the noise figure is less than or equal to 2.23dB, the output power at 1dB is better than 20dBm, and the test results are very consistent with the simulation.

articleTitle: A low-power, high-efficiency charge pump circuit for the coexistence of multiple charge pumps in 55 nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In intelligent mobile devices, a memory circuit is one of the important modules, charge pump circuit can provide the necessary high voltage for memory. This paper presents a charge pump circuit fabricated in the SMIC 55 nm BCD CMOS process to improve the working efficiency and reduce the power consumption of the circuit. The charge pump circuit designed in this paper takes into account the bulk effect of the transistor, and employs a dynamic substrate bias circuit in combination with a transmission transistor to eliminate the impact of the bulk effect on the threshold voltage; the clock circuit generates the staggered phase clock with double voltage output, reduces the influence of threshold voltage, and improves the working efficiency of charge pump circuit. Compared with the traditional charge pump circuit, this paper also considers the problem of excessive peak-to-peak current caused by multiple charge pumps working simultaneously. This article enables different charge pump circuits to be alternately turned on, to reduce the transient power consumption of the charge pump start; flip-flops capture and generate charge pump feedback clocks with different phases, reducing power consumption during the dynamic stabilization phase of the charge pump. Simulation results show that the charge pump circuit designed in this paper can meet the requirements of low power consumption and high efficiency when multiple charge pumps work simultaneously.

articleTitle: Research on Secure Storage with SATA Command Filtering Based on Logical Isolation Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: With the development of information technology, the importance of data security has been continuously increasing. Current research on data security mainly focuses on network security, host security, and application security, with relatively less attention given to storage security. As one of the carriers of storage systems and data, SATA solid-state drives (SSDs) are vulnerable to malicious code that can infect the SSD firmware and boot sectors, enabling unauthorized access to and tampering with sensitive user data, interfering with normal disk read/write operations, and causing data leakage, data corruption, and degradation of disk performance, all of which pose a serious threat to secure data storage. SATA command filtering technology, which reviews all disk access behaviors based on whitelist rules, can prevent malicious code from infecting the disk. Compared with other malicious code protection methods, SATA command filtering technology places a greater emphasis on real-time protection, offering real-time security for storage. To study its ability to protect against malicious code, this paper designs a secure storage SoC based on a logical isolation architecture, which is connected between the host and the hard drive. The firmware of the SoC maintains a whitelist of SATA commands, and a simulation environment is established to verify its functionality. The simulation results show that the SoC can identify the disk partition format without affecting communication between the host and the disk, filter malicious code firmware update behaviors and boot sector tampering, and prevent the infection of the hard disk by malicious code.

articleTitle: Research on Direction Finding Error Analysis Based on Passive Sonar Buoy Array
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: The passive sonar buoy direction finding error determines the cross positioning accuracy of the sonar buoy array. At present, passive sonar buoy arrays often ignore the actual changes in passive direction finding errors during cross positioning, resulting in overly ideal cross positioning errors. The passive direction finding error is usually affected by factors such as formula approximation, measurement error, buoy deployment error, and buoy position deviation with waves. In response to the above issues, the basic principle of passive direction finding applicable to passive sonar buoy arrays was first introduced. Secondly, the approximate formula error, measurement error, float deployment error, and float position deviation error were analyzed. Finally, the impact of four types of errors on the cross positioning of passive sonar buoy arrays was simulated, and suggestions for improving the accuracy of cross positioning were provided.

articleTitle: Reversible Information Hiding Algorithm Based on Multi-MSB Histogram Shift
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Among the reversible data hiding (RDH) algorithms, histogram shift (HS) is simple and relatively high security, due to its advantage of low algorithmic complexity is suitable for lightweight systems, based on this this paper proposes a reversible information hiding method based on the improved histogram shift algorithm. The method divides the complete reversible information hiding process into three phases including predictor selection, pixel selection, and embedding algorithm. Predictor period selection refers to selecting the most applicable prediction method based on the texture structure of the image considering the accuracy and reversibility of the prediction. Pixel selection refers to prioritizing the pixels that are in the smoothing region, and the PSNR of the image can still be kept high after embedding the information. The embedding algorithm of the method can adaptively use the multi-MSBs of the original pixel value and the predicted pixel value to obtain the prediction error, and realize the embedding of pixel values by the multi-expanded bin histogram shifting algorithm. The advantages of this method are (1) Unlike the complete pixel values, the predicted values of the multi-MSBs are more accurate, and a smaller prediction error can be obtained even in rough regions. (2) The use of multi-extended bin histogram shifting algorithm can realize the increase of embedding capacity without increasing the algorithm complexity. (3) The predictor can be selected adaptively according to the image texture. After the experiment, it can be proved that the method can realize larger capacity of information embedding under the guarantee of higher PSNR.

articleTitle: Research on Wireless Battery Management System Based on Bluetooth
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: With the rapid increase in the use of electric vehicles and renewable energy storage systems, the demand for batteries has also increased. These systems require more efficient and intelligent battery management technologies to optimize battery performance and extend battery life. The traditional wired Battery Management System design is complex and requires a large number of data transmission lines to communicate with the battery pack. In response to the problem of complex communication wiring harnesses in battery management systems, this paper designs a wireless battery management system (WBMS) based on Bluetooth star network, which controls and manages battery packs through wireless communication via Bluetooth, replacing wired communication and reducing wiring harnesses. Considering the high cost and efficiency issues of traditional battery balancing methods, this paper proposes a wireless reconfigurable balancing method that uses the switching characteristics of MOSFETs instead of traditional equalizers to achieve battery balancing

articleTitle: CTSA : Tree Seed Algorithm Improved with Cyclic Mutation Spiral Mixing Mechanism and New Crossover Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Based on the limitations of the Tree Seed Algorithm (TSA), such as its proneness to getting trapped in local optima and its relatively slow convergence speed, this study proposes an improved TSA optimization algorithm - the Tree Seed Algorithm improved by the periodic mutation spiral hybrid mechanism and a new crossover strategy (CTSA). The CTSA incorporates periodic mutation and helical mixing mechanisms, which significantly enhance the algorithm's local search capabilities and its ability to escape local optima, thus mitigating TSA's tendency to converge prematurely to suboptimal solutions. Additionally, we introduce a novel inter-species crossover strategy that markedly improves the algorithm's global search efficiency. Through comparative experiments, the CTSA has demonstrated superior optimization capabilities and faster convergence speeds compared to several benchmark algorithms, including Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Adaptive Tree Seed Algorithm (ATSA), Modified Tree Seed Algorithm (MTSA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Biogeography-Based Optimization (BOA).

articleTitle: A metasurface-based Circularly Polarized Transmitarray Antenna Element Used in Satellite Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In this paper, a metasurface-based circularly polarized transmitarray antenna element used in satellite Communication is proposed. This element adopts a single-layer square 4×4 metasurface and a double-layer angular 4×4 metasurface to realize linear polarization to circular polarization conversion, which can reflect y-polarized wave, transmit xpolarized wave and convert it into circular polarized wave. This element has good matching characteristics and circular polarization characteristics. At the same time, 360 ° phase compensation is realized by changing the phase delay line. This element has low insertion loss, and can realize linear phase in a wide frequency band. The structure is simple to process and the cost is low, so that it can be mass-produced.

articleTitle: A data processing method applied to a real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR instrument
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Since the outbreak of the novel coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) in 2019, nucleic acid test results have become a crucial basis for identifying and isolating infected individuals, thereby limiting the further spread of the pandemic. To achieve accurate quantitative analysis of nucleic acid test results, this paper proposes an enhanced fluorescence signal processing method. First, Gaussian fitting [11] is employed to extract the peak values of the fluorescence signals. Subsequently, the signals are further optimized through a combination of polynomial interpolation, smoothing techniques, and a five-point moving average filter. Finally, the PCR amplification curve is modeled using a four-parameter logistic fitting [12], and the Ct value is precisely calculated by determining the intersection between the threshold line and the fitted curve. This approach demonstrates superior effectiveness in processing raw data, significantly improving the detection performance of the optical system, and providing valuable insights for the data processing methods of rotary-based real-time quantitative PCR instruments.

articleTitle: GPR Image Denoising Based on Improved DNCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) images are often affected by Gaussian noise, which reduces their clarity. While traditional filtering methods can mitigate noise to some extent, they often struggle to preserve image details simultaneously. Deep learning-based Denoising Convolutional Neural Network (DNCNN) has demonstrated notable performance in image denoising, yet its effectiveness in handling Gaussian noise in GPR images leaves room for improvement. This study enhances the DNCNN model by integrating a Bottleneck Attention Module (BAM) module, enabling the network to better identify and focus on both noise and image details, thereby improving denoising performance. Experimental results show that the modified DNCNN model not only surpasses traditional techniques but also outperforms the original DNCNN in GPR image denoising. The improvements in PSNR and SSIM metrics confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[3]</sup>.

articleTitle: Applicability analysis of new power system protection considering the fault characteristics of DFIG
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: As the power grid continues to evolve, the emerging power system exhibits "dual high" characteristics, characterized by a high penetration rate of renewable energy sources and a high proportion of power electronic devices. When wind power generators with high permeability are integrated into the distribution network, their intricate magnetic transient behaviors can lead to malfunctions or unintended tripping of existing relay protection schemes. This paper specifically examines the Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) and assesses its compatibility with distribution network protection strategies. Firstly, the transient characteristics of DFIG during distribution network faults were analyzed, followed by an analysis of its applicability for current protection when connected to the distribution network. Finally, a power grid structure with DFIG was built in PSCAD, and tests were conducted separately for faults at the access point and downstream faults. The results indicate that when a fault occurs in the power line, it may cause the protection range of the lower level quick break protection at the connection location to expand or even exceed the limit. At the same time, due to the low frequency characteristic of the doubly fed fan, it may cause the upper level current differential protection at the connection location to refuse to operate.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of HOE for Holographic Display System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This paper proposes the design and optimization of holographic optical element (HOE) for holographic display systems. A novel HOE is designed, fabricated, and optimized to replace traditional lenses, reducing system size and cost. Additionally, random phase plates (RPPs) are introduced to suppress noise and improve image quality. Experimental results demonstrate that the HOE achieves a maximum diffraction efficiency of approximately 60% under optimal angle and exposure time. The incorporation of RPPs enhances the structural similarity index (SSIM) of reconstructed images from 0.40 to 0.58, improving image clarity and uniformity significantly. These results provide a practical solution for developing compact and high-performance holographic display systems.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis of Cardiovascular Disease under Double-Layer Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major contributor to the current rise in mortality rates, so accurate prediction of CVD is crucial. Traditional prediction methods often rely on a single type of data, ignoring the complementarity between different modalities of information. This study proposed a multi-modal deep learning framework using ResNet-BiLSTM to extract ECG features and Graph Neural Networks (GNN) to extract clinical data features. Two static and dynamic attention mechanisms were added to optimize the fusion of multi-modal features. The experimental results show that the proposed method performs better than traditional models in terms of accuracy, F1 score, and AUC [1].

articleTitle: Design of Sub-band Cooperative Beamforming for Onboard Digital Transparent Processor
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: A sub-band cooperative beamforming method is proposed for onboard digital transparent processor, which may be affected in orbit by the harsh electromagnetic environment. In the proposed scheme, several discrete sub-bands are cooperative to retransmit the signal, which are assigned independent gain adjustment coefficient. Under the criterion of maximizing the signal-to-noise ratio of the ground receiver, a mathematical model is established for optimizing the received signal-to-noise ratio. The proposed sub-band cooperative beamforming scheme can effectively utilize the interfered spectrum resources, improve the system outage performance and reduce the impact of interference on normal communications for digital transparent processor.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Receiver Equalization Circuit Based on Source Degeneration Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In the SerDes high-speed serial communication system, in order to eliminate the impact of non-ideal characteristics such as reflection, crosstalk and jitter, it is necessary to introduce an equalization circuit in the system to eliminate losses such as inter-code crosstalk. SerDes is often used in a variety of protocols, including high-speed protocols and low-speed protocols. In the case of low-speed protocols, we often use DFE plus CTLE structure, which consumes a lot of power. To address this problem, this paper proposes a low-power structure receiver equalization circuit. This circuit is based on the UMC28nm CMOS process. This circuit structure consists of three first-level traditional non-adjustable CTLEs, a two-level CTLE and a current mode structure weighted circuit. The non-adjustable CTLE structure is used for fixed gain equalization adjustment, and adaptive adjustment is achieved by adjusting the current copied by the current mirror in the current mode structure. Compared with the traditional adaptive CTLE structure, the adjustable resistor and capacitor array are reduced, which greatly reduces power consumption.

articleTitle: Design of FPGA-based PCIe_SRIO conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In order to meet the data interaction between PCIe bus and SRIO bus, a PCIe_SRIO conversion design with flexibility and portability based on FPGA implementation is studied. The design is based on the PCIe interface to realize the interaction between the CPU chip and the FPGA chip. The FPGA realizes the mutual conversion between the PCIe interface and the SRIO interface and distributes the data to multiple SRIO devices for processing through the SRIO switch. This paper also introduces the architecture of this PCIe_SRIO conversion design, describes in detail the functions of each module of the architecture, and gives the functional simulation as well as test result. The achievement solves the interface conversion problem between PCIe interface and SRIO interface, which is a reference for inter-board data transmission.

articleTitle: Research on Task Offloading Strategies in Edge Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Edge computing fulfills the urgent need of users for low-latency and high-quality computing services by transferring tasks from end devices to the edge side of the network for processing through task offloading techniques. However, edge computing still faces many challenges during task offloading. Considering that most task offloading strategies only optimize a single objective, this paper constructs a multi-objective optimization task offloading model, which integrates multiple metrics such as task offloading failure rate, task processing time, and load balancing. In order to solve the optimal solution of this model, this paper proposes a hybrid meta-heuristic algorithm based on greedy random adaptive search procedure (GRASP) and genetic algorithm (GA), called GAGRA. experimental results show that compared with genetic algorithm, ant colony algorithm, and simulated annealing algorithm, GAGRA enhances the task offloading failure rate, the task processing time, and load balancing respectively by 4.28%, 4.94% and 5.02%. These results validate the effectiveness of the task offloading strategy proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Adaptive Optimization of Shield Tunnel Segment Assembly Points by Integrating DBSCAN and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In shield tunnel construction, segment assembly is a critical process, and its quality directly affects the overall performance and safety of the tunnel. Although the technology for shield tunnel segment assembly has developed, it still has limitations. Traditional methods for selecting assembly points often rely on experience or simple rules, making it difficult to adapt to the complex and dynamic construction environment.Genetic algorithms are widely used in optimization problems, and some studies have applied them to weight optimization for segment assembly point selection. However, existing methods often use fixed interval classification, which lacks flexibility and cannot dynamically adjust based on the actual data distribution. This leads to classification errors, particularly when dealing with unevenly distributed data.To address these issues, this paper proposes an innovative method that integrates DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) and genetic algorithms, aiming to achieve adaptive optimization of shield tunnel segment assembly points. The goal is to improve the accuracy and adaptability of assembly point selection, thereby enhancing tunnel construction quality.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern of a VLF Multi-Fed Linear Antenna in an Anisotropic Magnetoplasma
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In this paper, the radiation pattern of a very low frequency (VLF) multi-feed linear antenna in a magnetoplasma exhibiting anisotropy is determined and discussed with the help of the semi-analytical method. By taking account of the complex anisotropic property of the surrounding medium, the closed-form solution of the radiation field induced by the antenna is given first. By solving the integrals contained in the expression, the field distributions in both the near and far zones are shown and analyzed. The theoretical findings presented in this work could contribute to optimizing the performance of realistic VLF satellite-based radiation systems.

articleTitle: A Novel Multiobjective Design Technique for LTCC Bandpass Filters with Fractal-Shaped Segments
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new technique for designing bandpass filters based on low-temperature cofired ceramic (LTCC) technology. The proposed method innovatively represents the conductor shape contour of the LTCC bandpass filter with nodes and segments. By defining the distributed nodes' positions, the cross-plane line segment structure with fractal shapes, and applying appropriate node connection schemes, A bandpass filtering structure that ensures effective transmission of in-band signals and effective out-of-band suppression can be constructed. By encoding the shape attributes of nodes and line segments, as well as well-defined multiple objective functions, the multiobjective evolutionary algorithm can be utilized for the optimization design for the proposed filter.

articleTitle: Underwater Digital Image Stabilization Using Optical Flow Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of irregular camera jitter caused by water flow impacts during underwater shaking table tests. A digital image stabilization method based on optical flow is proposed to mitigate this problem. The method consists of the following parts: (1) Segmentation of the moving background and foreground to identify the region to be stabilized; (2) Detection and tracking of target feature points within this region using optical flow for motion estimation; (3) Elimination of mismatched feature points using histogram-based thresholding; (4) Compensation of jitter vectors to generate a stabilized image sequence. Both quantitative and qualitative analyses demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method. Experimental results indicate that the method significantly reduces measurement errors caused by camera jitter, controlling the error at a sub-pixel level.

articleTitle: A Tiny Processor with Rapid Interrupt Response for AI Accelerator Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an ultra-compact RISC-V–based processor optimized for low power consumption, minimal size, and rapid interrupt response, specifically targeting the control of AI accelerators. The proposed processor incorporates two key innovations: a simplified architecture for managing external IPs and a dedicated fast interrupt response controller. These features result in a streamlined core and reduced interrupt handling latency, making the processor highly suitable for real-time applications such as embedded AI systems and edge computing. The rapid interrupt response mechanism ensures that external interrupts are handled within four clock cycles for non-nested interrupts and non-jump instructions. When implemented on an FPGA, the proposed processor reduces hardware overhead compared to picoRV32, achieving a 20.7% decrease in Slice LUTs and a 27.9% reduction in Slice Registers. Simulation results using the CMOS 65nm process demonstrate a 31.7% reduction in area and a 26.7% decrease in power consumption, while task execution efficiency is only reduced by 1.68%.

articleTitle: CSTLineDP: A Fine-grained Software Defect Prediction Framework Based on CST and Bi-GRU
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Software defect detection based on deep learning technology is an important research field. However, there are still obvious limitations in the existing research: (1) most of the current research is coarse-grained, and code defects can only be located at the coarse-grained level, such as function level and file level; (2) existing methods rely more on the code text, ignoring the use of code structure information, resulting in low predict accuracy. (3) the risk score of each code token cannot be obtained, resulting in insufficient interpretability of the prediction results. Aiming at the shortcomings of previous studies, we propose CSTLineDP, which combines the hierarchical structure information of the code (based on the concrete syntax tree) with the text information to achieve fine-grained and interpretable code defect prediction. Experimental results on the public Java and C/C++ datasets indicate that, compared with other baseline methods, our method improves the three evaluation indicators by 8.8% ~ 32.2%, 1.5% ~ 16.0% and 13 ~ 27, respectively.

articleTitle: Optimization of return link carrier planning for brandband GEO satellite communications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: To enhance resource utilization in GEO satellite return links, this paper proposes a novel dynamic carrier configuration optimization algorithm (CCOA) to address the carrier planning and allocation problem in Ka/Ku-band broadband satellite networks. Under throughput and outage probability constraints, CCOA dynamically adjusts carrier allocation based on rain attenuation levels by grouping user traffic, adapting to the time-varying channel conditions. SNS3 simulation results demonstrate a 9% reduction in total bandwidth occupancy and a significant decrease in packet loss rate under rain attenuation.

articleTitle: Human-Computer Interaction in Smart Devices: Leveraging Sentiment Analysis and Knowledge Graphs for Personalized User Experiences
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This study proposes a user experience analysis method for smart devices based on user behavior pattern analysis and device response optimization, aiming to improve the response accuracy and user satisfaction of smart devices in human-computer interaction. Through the collection of interaction data between users and smart devices, the study delves into the application of sentiment analysis and knowledge graphs within smart devices. This research analyzes user behavior patterns, emotional shifts, and the device’s response strategies. The experimental results show that by optimizing the device response strategy, not only the response accuracy is improved but also the user satisfaction is significantly improved. In particular, when the device can make personalized feedback according to the user's emotional changes, the interaction effect is significantly improved. In addition, the experiment also verifies the device's responsiveness under different emotional states, demonstrating the optimized device's accurate understanding and intelligent response to user needs. This study provides new ideas for emotional perception, demand prediction, and personalized interaction design of smart devices, and lays a theoretical foundation for future user experience optimization based on artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Maize Growth Simulation Analysis and Yield Prediction Based on Integrated Learning Algorithm and WOFOST Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Maize growth status and yield prediction are the key issues in maize planting management. Traditional prediction methods rely on single crop growth models or machine learning algorithms, which have the problems of insufficient prediction accuracy and limited adaptability. The combination of ensemble learning and crop model provides a new idea for improving the prediction accuracy. In this study, an improved maize growth prediction model was proposed based on the WOFOST model, combined with the irrigation model and the ensemble learning algorithm. By introducing K-means clustering and data assimilation technology, the model parameters were optimized to improve the prediction performance. The experimental data are derived from NASA's meteorological data from 1990 to 2020, and the results show that the improved model performs well in the prediction of key indicators such as leaf area index, soil water content and total biomass, and its MAE and MSE are reduced to 2.836 and 7.581, respectively, with a coefficient of determination R—2 It is improved to 0.942, which is significantly better than the traditional WOFOST model and other machine learning algorithms, demonstrating the efficiency and reliability of the improved model in maize growth prediction.

articleTitle: A Behavior Prediction and Comparison Method for IoT Device Trustworthiness Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, ensuring their security and trustworthiness has become an urgent challenge. This study presents a novel network behavior prediction method leveraging the Transformer model, specifically designed to assess the credibility of IoT devices. Unlike traditional models, our approach uniquely combines advanced deep learning techniques with a custom algorithm to evaluate device trustworthiness. The Transformer model predicts future behaviors based on historical network activities, and these predictions are compared with actual activities to calculate similarities and discrepancies. This process quantifies device trustworthiness, allowing us to determine their reliability against predefined thresholds. The results demonstrate that our model achieves a high accuracy of 92.7% in predicting network behavior after training on 50,324 data entries, representing significant improvements of 3.4%, 44.7%, and 43.6% over LSTM, SVM, and LR models, respectively. Furthermore, our method maintains an accuracy rate of over 90% in identifying untrustworthy devices even under attack conditions (DoS, MITM, Malware). Our findings offer a robust solution to a critical problem, making a significant contribution to the field of IoT security.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of AM Signal Modulation and Demodulation System Based on STM32 and ZYNQ
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This article focuses on taking the STM32F407ZGT6 single-chip microcomputer and the four-channel DDS AD9959 as the core. Combined with the serial port screen, the modulation degree and carrier frequency can be set. For the modulated signal, it is sampled by the AD9481 module and transmitted to the PL side of ZYNQ for demodulation and then the modulated signal is output. The data is transmitted to the PS side and the modulation degree is calculated, and finally transmitted to the upper computer. After testing, the system can realize signal modulation and demodulation when the carrier frequency is 30 - 40MHZ and the modulation signal frequency is 10KHZ. The demodulated waveform has no distortion and the modulation degree error is no more than 3%.

articleTitle: Multiscale Convolutional Attention Network for Epileptic Seizure Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Timely and accurate prediction of epileptic seizures allows healthcare professionals to implement interventions promptly prior to a seizure, preventing secondary injuries. Many previous deep learning network models have achieved varying degrees of success in seizure prediction. However, most of the existing prediction models do not fully extract and integrate the temporal and spatial feature information in multichannel electroencephalogram (EEG). To address this issue, this study proposes a multiscale convolutional attention network for epileptic seizure prediction. Specifically, the network consists of a weighted attention mechanism and a multiscale convolutional module, which are designed respectively for highlighting the spatial information in important EEG channels and capturing both the local and the global temporal features. Tested on the CHB-MIT scalp EEG dataset, the seizure prediction method based on the multiscale convolutional attention network achieved an average sensitivity of 97.5%, an average false prediction rate of 0.30/h, and an average prediction time of 26.04 minutes. The results of multiple experiments further validate the feature extraction capability to multichannel EEG and the seizure prediction performance of the multiscale convolutional attention network.

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation of a communication network with Transmission Distance Constraint
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Considering transmission distance constraint, a reliability evaluation method is proposed to evaluate the data transmission capability of a communication network in an uncertain environment. Network reliability is defined as the probability that the amount of data transmitted by the network can meet the requirements of devices when each edge has random transmission capacity and there is a limit on the transmission distance. By utilizing the concept of the minimal path, a reliability model based on minimal capacity vector is established, and an effective calculation method is designed. Finally, the results of numerical experiments show that the data transmission distance has a significant impact on the reliability of a communication network, and this impact is even greater under high demand levels.

articleTitle: Research on Secure Communication Methods for High-Speed Cross-Network Data Exchange
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This paper introduces the application requirements for high-speed secure communication across networks, the fundamental principles of cross-network data exchange, and its implementation. Based on high-speed switch technology and proprietary protocols, a hardware-software co-design solution is proposed to achieve secure communication for cross-network data exchange. The solution eliminates potential security risks associated with unauthorized access, intrusion attacks, and information leakage in heterogeneous network interconnections. It establishes robust defense capabilities against illegal network intrusions, attacks, and failures, meeting the security communication requirements for controlled interconnection and cross-network data exchange between specialized networks.

articleTitle: Research on Industrial Internet Data Collection Application Based on Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This study designed an edge computing system based on Raspberry Pi, which improved the real-time and effectiveness of industrial data through data collection, processing algorithms and model simulation. The system uses industrial protocols to realize data collection from multiple sensors, and completes preliminary data processing and feature extraction through the algorithm module of the edge node. The simulation part uses precise data analysis technology to evaluate the system performance. The results show that the scheme performs well in terms of latency and bandwidth occupancy, and significantly reduces the data transmission load. The reliability and scalability of the edge computing system based on Raspberry Pi in complex industrial environments have been verified. Through the research and implementation of this system, the application potential of Raspberry Pi in industrial Internet data collection is demonstrated, which provides a technical reference for the further development of intelligent manufacturing and lays the foundation for the promotion and application of edge computing in the industrial field.

articleTitle: Design of an Intelligent Flood Control Inspection well System Based on Pseudorange Differential Joint Carrier Phase Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Aiming at the technical problem of insufficient positioning accuracy in monitoring and early warning of urban flooding, the research on the optimization of pseudo-range difference algorithm, the application of carrier phase algorithm, and the research on Internet of Things and big data processing technology is carried out from the introduction of high-precision positioning technology, the real-time monitoring of the water level in inspection wells, and the fusion of data [1]. Using the pseudorange difference combined with carrier phase algorithm, big data analysis platform and other technical methods, the system realizes the high-precision determination of inspection well position, real-time monitoring and warning of water level, and intelligent processing and analysis of data. The system simulation experiment was carried out by applying professional simulation software, and when an abnormal situation occurs, it is able to send out warning information in time to remind the management personnel to manage [2]. The results show that the technical solution of intelligent flood prevention inspection well system based on pseudo-range differential joint carrier phase algorithm has feasibility and effectiveness in improving the efficiency of urban flood monitoring and early warning.

articleTitle: Ground-based microwave radiometer with high precision double channels
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: A new ground-based high precision double-channel microwave radiometer MWR-120-PCFE for atmospheric remote sensing is designed. The microwave radiometer adopts Peltier cooling front-end technology to increase stability, reduce the system noise, improve the sensitivity and signal quality. The dual-channel design provides the simultaneous measurement of microwave radiation at 110/115 GHz of two molecules, which improves the measurement efficiency. The use parabolic quasioptic system, integrated IF module makes the radiometer more compact and portable, reducing cost and complexity. The innovation and improvement of this microwave radiometer in technology makes it have a wider application prospect in the fields of atmosphere physics, meteorology, remote sensing, and provides greater convenience and efficiency for scientific research and practical applications.

articleTitle: Research of 800Gbit/s OSFP DR8 Silicon Photonics Optical Transceiver Module
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In today’s era of rapid technological development, cutting-edge technologies such as cloud computing and artificial intelligence are continuously advancing. As a critical component of data transmission, the optical communication industry has entered a stage of comprehensive and rapid growth. To effectively meet the demands of modern data center systems for high-speed data transmission, this paper proposes a design for an 800 Gbit/s silicon photonic transceiver module. First, the paper explains the working principles and components of the 800 Gbit/s silicon photonic transceiver module. The four key components of the module—transmission, reception, control, and digital signal processing—are introduced and analyzed. Through performance testing of the module’s transmission and reception capabilities, it is verified that the proposed design meets the required performance specifications. This work provides a practical 800 Gbit/s solution for Ethernet transmission in data centers.

articleTitle: Design and application of intelligent edge terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: With the continuous development of 5G technology and the large-scale connection of new energy, traditional power terminals can no longer meet new business needs such as real-time energy and refined load management of electricity users. Therefore, based on the business needs of major scenarios such as smart home appliances, smart buildings, and smart parks, this paper carries out the development of intelligent edge terminals (IEU), realizing high-frequency collection of massive energy consumption data based on 5G communication technology. It introduces D2D technology to build communication links between terminals, which further enhances data transmission rate. At the same time, it realizes load identification and load prediction based on the edge computing capabilities. It also realizes real-time regulation and management of load resources to achieve intelligent monitoring of electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Train Autonomous Positioning Based on Visible Light Imaging Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Accurate position information is a key factor in ensuring the safe operation of trains in communication-based train control (CBTC) systems. To improve the real-time performance and accuracy of positioning, an autonomous positioning method based on visible light imaging communication is proposed. First, the LED light source is modulated to carry a identifier (ID) corresponding to the information. A CMOS camera, located at the top front of the train, captures real-time images of the LED light source. Next, the sampling technique is used to detect the region of interest of the LED light source, obtaining its position information. Finally, the train's position is accurately calculated based on the camera's imaging principles. Experimental results show that the proposed method can provide excellent positioning services for CBTC systems based on train-to-train communication.

articleTitle: Local Bounds for Incentive Compatible Selection Mechanisms in Forests
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: We studied the incentive-compatible selection mechanisms for directed forests. A directed forest is an acyclic directed graph with maximum out-degree equal to 1. A selection mechanism gives a probability distribution on each vertex in the forest. A selection mechanism is incentive-compatible (IC), if the probability assigned to a vertex does not change when it changes which it points to (or add, delete the edge).An IC mechanism is fair if the probability of a vertex is always larger then the one with less vertices with access to itself, and the probability of a vertex is always equal to the one with the same number of vertices with access to itself. An IC mechanism is exact if the sum of the probability of each vertex is always 1.The quality of a selection mechanism is the worst-case ratio between the expected number with access to each vertex and the maximum number with access to a vertex. The upper bound is decided by a special case and the lower bound is decided by a mechanism. In this paper, we focus on the local case for this question, i.e. n = 2, 3.We prove that for n = 2, the tight bound of quality for IC, fair and exact mechanisms are all 0.8. For n = 3, IC mechanisms achieve a bound of quality [7/9, 0.8]. However, fair mechanisms achieve a bound of quality [0.6, 0.8] and exact mechanisms achieve a tight bound 7/9.

articleTitle: An Efficient Direct Access Algorithm for Integer Compression
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In our previous work [1], we introduced a technique for reordering prefix codes, enabling direct access functionality without the need for additional storage. In this paper, we extend our previous work [1] into integer compression. Concurrently, we minimized the bit count required for random access reads. We first restructured the codeword of the variable-length quantity (VLQ) code, allowing the determination of the codeword's length through its prefix. In addition, an efficient direct access algorithm for the reorganized VLQ code is given. The simulation outcomes indicate that in scenarios where the encoded stream prohibits the allocation of extra space, the proposed method results in a reduction of bits per access read by more than three orders of magnitude and is 4× less than both the conventional VLQ scheme and the current solution.

articleTitle: Multimodal model for pneumonia detection based on enhanced stacking MOE
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence technology for pneumonia detection has always been an important topic in medical imaging, and integrating and processing various medical data sources to enhance the early diagnosis and identification of pneumonia has become a key challenge in the healthcare field. This study proposes a novel pneumonia prediction model with a hybrid architecture, which integrates the most advanced large language models and a stacking MOE architecture. The model combines the pre-trained ResNet-50 on ImageNet for effective image feature extraction, while using BERT to extract and analyze textual data from patient self-reports. This study uses a small-scale dataset to test pneumonia prediction based on X-ray images and patient self-reported text. The experimental results show that the hybrid model outperforms the single-modality models in all evaluation metrics. Additionally, this study conducted an ablation test on the stacking MOE and LLMs components, demonstrating the effectiveness of each component. The research results provide a feasible approach for the potential of multimodal artificial intelligence models in accurately detecting pneumonia and contribute to the development of flexible clinical diagnostic tools.

articleTitle: Waveform Design of Integrated Communication and Navigation System in High Dynamic Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: High-dynamic scenarios pose significant challenges to the stability and performance of integrated communication and navigation (ICAN) systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a frame structure for an anti-high-dynamic ICAN system, enabling high-precision navigation and reliable communication even under high-speed motion and complex Doppler shifts. A preamble sequence is designed for coarse frequency offset estimation, while pilot sequences are utilized for fine frequency offset estimation. This approach effectively mitigates the impact of Doppler frequency offsets on the ICAN system, providing both a theoretical foundation and technical support for the application of ICAN technology in complex scenarios. Simulation results validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed frame structure.

articleTitle: Image Data Fusion Based on Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In this paper, the image data fusion and evaluation based on wavelet transform are studied, the appropriate number of decomposition layers and wavelet types are selected, and four fusion rules are formulated for the decomposed high-frequency coefficient and low-frequency coefficient, and the feature-level image data fusion is completed. MATLAB software has been used to simulate the image fusion of plant set images and animal set images, and the fusion effect was evaluated by using color features, texture features, mean and variance indicators. The experimental results demonstrate that the image fusion effect is better when the fusion rule selects the largest high-frequency component and the average low-frequency component. The research on image fusion data based on wavelet transform can obtain high-quality fusion images based on multi-source images, which is of great significance to improve the utilization rate of image information and expand the application scenarios of images.

articleTitle: Aerial Image Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOV8s
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: With the rapid development of drone technology, target detection based on drones has become a hot spot in current research. However, existing methods face challenges such as low detection accuracy and poor real-time performance. To address this problem, an improved target detection method YOLOV8s-SME is proposed for application in aerial images. This algorithm combines the lightweight StarNet backbone network, replaces the traditional feature pyramid network, and uses the multi-scale feature fusion module (MFFM). In addition, EUCB's upsampling strategy and Dsmehead are used to improve detection accuracy. Experimental results show that on the Visdrone2019 data set, YOLOV8s-SEM significantly reduces the amount of parameters and calculations while maintaining detection accuracy. The inference speed and post-processing time are superior to traditional methods, and is suitable for drones with limited computing resources. Real-time target detection applications on the device.

articleTitle: An Integrated Multi-Sensor Fusion Architecture for Advanced Laboratory Security Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: As the number of university laboratories continues to increase, laboratory safety issues are becoming increasingly prominent. Safety threats such as fires and theft pose serious challenges to the safety of personnel and property. To address the problems existing in the security systems of most university laboratories, this study has designed an intelligent security alarm system that has dual functions of fire detection and safety monitoring. The system uses temperature and humidity sensors, light intensity sensors, and smoke concentration sensors to determine whether to trigger a fire alarm. At the same time, it employs fingerprint recognition sensors and button password input to decide whether to activate the security alarm. If the collected data for temperature, humidity, light intensity, and smoke concentration exceeds the set thresholds, a buzzer and LED indicator light will issue an alarm signal. If the fingerprint information or password is entered incorrectly more than three times, the buzzer will also sound an alarm. The system allows personnel with administrative privileges to modify passwords or add new fingerprint information. In addition, the system transmits data to a mini-program through a communication module and a cloud platform, enabling administrators to remotely monitor the operating status and safety conditions of the system in real-time, so that potential safety hazards can be identified and addressed promptly. The intelligent security alarm system provides comprehensive protection for laboratory safety, helps to enhance the safety of laboratory personnel and equipment, and prevents significant losses.

articleTitle: Research on intelligent monitoring and optimization control system model of greenhouse environment based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This paper presents an improved intelligent control model for greenhouse environments, integrating environmental monitoring data with a deep learning approach combining multilayer CNN and LSTM networks with model predictive control (MPC). By optimizing model parameters and utilizing data fusion techniques, the system’s prediction accuracy and response speed are enhanced. Experimental results from a real greenhouse monitoring system show that the improved model significantly outperforms traditional models and other machine learning algorithms, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.342, mean square error (MSE) of 6.749, and a coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) of 0.931, demonstrating its efficiency and reliability in controlling key environmental indicators like temperature, humidity, and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Optimization of Stacked Chip Macro-Module Layout Based on Memristor-Inspired Evolutionary Game
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: As the complexity of chip design continues to increase, the stacking of multiple device layers in a three dimension(3D) architecture has emerged as a promising approach, which aims to optimize the placement and interconnections of large function blocks across the vertically-stacked device layers. Due to the complex interactions between layout and design constraints, traditional deterministic optimization often struggle to navigate its multi-modal search landscape effectively. Thus, we creatively propose the memristive evolutionary game: the diverse metal layers engage in a strategic interplay that determines the ownership hierarchy of chip macro modules and the 2D layout of these chip macro modules within each designated metal layer is orchestrated using evolutionary algorithm, which harness the power of game theoretic evolution to seek the optimal solution, balancing the objectives of minimizing layout area and wiring length. Upon comparison with alternative algorithms, the game evolution algorithm introduced in this paper exhibits superior optimization performance.

articleTitle: Improved AES scheme based on chaotic mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: As encryption algorithms are widely used, the shortcomings of Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) round keys with strong correlation between them have also been found. In this paper, an improved AES scheme based on Logistic mapping and Tent mapping is proposed to use the random sequences generated by the two chaotic mappings to generate the wheel keys, and improve and optimize the original key expansion algorithm, which generates wheel keys without correlation among them, the key space is large enough, and the sequences and wheel keys are different each time, which enhances the ability of AES to withstand attacks. Through the security test analysis of random sequences, it shows that the improved AES can ensure the key expansion algorithm has enough security, solve the problem of wheel key correlation, and realize the effect of one secret at a time.

articleTitle: Data Processing and Sensor Data Fusion Algorithm Application in Smart Safety Helmets
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Aiming at the real-time and accuracy requirements of smart safety helmets for personnel status monitoring in complex environments, a multimodal data processing algorithm based on sensor data fusion is studied to improve the detection performance and response speed of safety helmets.
