Furthermore, the robustness and noise-resistance capabilities of the semi-supervised CNN model were validated through experiments under varying noise levels, confirming its practical applicability in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Cooperative Dynamic Task Allocation for Unmanned Surface Vehicle Swarms Based on CART Decision Trees
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: In common multi-boat task allocation, most of them adopt a global allocation method, which assigns all the tasks of the target to different unmanned boats for sequential execution at one time. However, in the ever-changing battlefield environment, there is a possibility that the unmanned boat will fail to perform the task. At this time, the target task needs to be allocated again, and a single global allocation cannot meet the task requirements. Therefore, based on the different types of target tasks, this paper adopts a cascade method and uses the Classification and Regression Tree(CART) to establish the classification model of the task target and the unmanned boat group respectively. According to the task requirements and task execution status, an event trigger is set up. When the event requirements are met, the improved crow search task allocation algorithm is called to update the task list of the specified unmanned boat. It not only solves the limitations of global allocation, but also improves the flexibility and adaptability of task allocation, ensuring that the unmanned boat group can complete the task efficiently and accurately in a complex and changing battlefield environment.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Transformer-Assisted Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation and Computation Offloading in 5G Private Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: The rapid development of 5G private networks has brought demands for ultra-low latency, high bandwidth, and high reliability. However, resource allocation and task scheduling in multi-task and multi-user scenarios still pose significant challenges. To address this, this paper proposes a blockchain-based and Transformer-assisted multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm for resource allocation and computation offloading optimization in 5G private networks. By constructing a total cost function that comprehensively considers task completion time, energy consumption, and service quality, and employing a multi-agent reinforcement learning method, each device can adaptively adjust its strategy. The Transformer model is introduced to effectively handle high-dimensional state information through its self-attention mechanism, enhancing the expressiveness and learning efficiency of the policy network. Combined with blockchain technology, the proposed method reduces the cost of blockchain operations while ensuring system security. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms baselines in terms of total cost, task completion time, energy consumption, and QoS satisfaction rate, validating its effectiveness and superiority.

articleTitle: Converter Transformer Fault Diagnosis Based on Domain Adaptive Semi-Supervision, Lightweight and Model Compression
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that deep learning cannot directly read one-dimensional dissolved gas data in oil, a wavelet transform data dimension conversion method based on the generalized Gaussian function is proposed to convert one-dimensional fault samples into two-dimensional The characteristic image is used to satisfy the data Diagnostic format of the converter transformer fault diagnosis method and at the same time, domain adaptive semi-supervised loss is introduced to optimize the model parameters. In view of the characteristics of existing deep learning models with many parameters and complex structures, a method based on lightweight neural networks and model compression is proposed to integrate and reduce deep learning models through convolutional layers and batch-normalization (BN) layers. The method of model compression by adjusting the bit-width of the parameters not only can effectively compress the deep learning model with almost no loss of model accuracy, but also improves the fault identification efficiency. In addition, the method can be successfully deployed on the edge computing platform, which realizes the effective utilization of resources and real-time response.

Author Keywords: fusion of convolution and batch normalization

articleTitle: Multi-organ CT Image Segmentation Model Based on Swin Transformer and CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: With the rapid development of medical imaging technology, Computed Tomography (CT) has become an indispensable tool in medical diagnosis. However, in the application of medical image segmentation, there are still some problems in CT images, such as the diversity of organ shape, size, location, texture, and interference factors like noise and artifacts. In response to these problems, this paper proposes a U-shaped medical image segmentation network STC-Unet based on a combination of CNN and Transformer. Based on the traditional U-Net with residual structure, the ST module improved by Swin Transformer was added, carry out global feature extraction and capture and be able to extract multi-scale spatial information, and add the Spatial Pyramid Pooling Coordinate Attention (SPP-CA) attention mechanism to the decoder to increase the module's ability to integrate spatial information. Relevant experiments were conducted on the Synapse multi-organ segmentation dataset. Experimental results show that STC-Unet has a DSC of 83.99% and HD95 of 15.59mm, achieving better segmentation results in multi-organ segmentation.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of vCPU Scheduling Architecture in Embedded Virtualization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel scheduling architecture designed for the independently developed Reworks hypervisor (Revmm), aimed at enhancing scheduling efficiency through static precomputation. The architecture integrates a configuration generation mechanism, enabling scheduling algorithms to leverage precomputed static results to assist dynamic scheduling decisions, thereby minimizing runtime overhead. Experimental results demonstrate that the statically precomputed Round-Robin algorithm surpasses traditional Round-Robin scheduling in terms of runtime efficiency and stability. To meet real-time requirements, the study also introduces a static priority-based, preemptible multicore VCPU scheduling algorithm (SPPM) for Revmm. Experiments confirm that this algorithm ensures stable real-time performance for the highest-priority RTOS.

articleTitle: Forecasting Cloud Workload through Reinforcement Learning-Based Ensemble Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: The escalating demand for cloud computing has intensified the need for accurate workload forecasting to optimize resource allocation and maintain service quality. This paper presents a novel approach employing a reinforcement learning-based ensemble model to enhance the accuracy of workload predictions in cloud environments. The study addresses the challenges posed by complex and dynamic workload patterns, leveraging deep learning techniques to improve prediction outcomes. The proposed model dynamically selects the optimal subset of predictors, demonstrating superior performance on the Google Cluster dataset. The research aims to contribute to more efficient and intelligent resource management in cloud computing.

articleTitle: Research on Construction Progress Monitoring Based on 3D Point Clouds and BIM Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Construction progress monitoring is a critical aspect of construction management. However, measuring the progress of a building remains a manual, time-consuming, and error-prone task that often involves lengthy analysis processes. These inefficiencies lead to delays, additional costs, and increased workloads. Effective progress monitoring requires comparing the planned construction state at a given time (planned state) with the actual construction state (as-built state). The planned state is typically derived from Building Information Modeling (BIM), which incorporates both the geometric design and the construction schedule, This paper proposes a point cloud projection method for coarse registration, leveraging the vertical alignment characteristics of buildings to the ground. Compared to traditional coarse registration methods, the proposed approach significantly improves both speed and accuracy. Following the registration of real-world point clouds with point clouds generated from BIM models, the method segments the point clouds into slabs and columns. By comparing their respective areas, the current construction progress is accurately calculated [1].

articleTitle: Research on Semantic Segmentation Method Based on Improved BiSeNetV2 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Leveraging the continuous advancements in fully convolutional networks, deep learning approaches have progressively superseded traditional image processing methods for low-level feature segmentation, thereby improving processing efficiency and enhancing the generalization ability of image segmentation. Semantic segmentation, in particular, refines pixel-level semantic information in annotated images, enriching perceptual map information and effectively enhancing system environmental understanding. Point cloud semantic maps, based on high-precision geometric maps, integrate fine-grained information from image semantic segmentation to achieve region-specific annotations, thereby enhancing the expressiveness of maps. As embedded devices for autonomous driving advance, lightweight and high real-time performance algorithms have become a new trend. Common segmentation models, such as encoder-decoder networks and dilated convolution networks, offer good segmentation accuracy but often face challenges with high memory usage and computational costs, making them less suitable for lightweight requirements in autonomous driving devices. BiSeNetV2, as a real-time semantic segmentation model with a bilateral structure, effectively balances segmentation accuracy, speed, and network complexity. Therefore, this paper enhances the BiSeNetV2 model by integrating the CBAM and ECA attention mechanisms and replacing the GSConv convolutional module, thereby improving the segmentation accuracy and robustness of the semantic segmentation network.

articleTitle: CLogLLM: A Large Language Model Enabled Approach to Cybersecurity Log Anomaly Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: Log data is commonly used to record the status of the system and the events that occur, which are often used to assist security staff to determine whether the system is abnormal, diagnose problems, troubleshooting. However, with the increasing complexity of the system, the log data becomes more and more numerous and complex, Therefore the analysis of the log becomes extremely difficult. Not coincidentally, with the emergence of various system software updates, traditional deep learning-based anomaly detection methods, which rely on pre-existing data for training, often struggle to maintain their effectiveness. At the same time, simply detecting anomalies in significant number of complex log data is no longer meet operational needs. Therefore, LLM which is capable of realizing zero-shot learning and text generation has attracted attention. This paper proposed method which is based on the implementation of LLMs for security log detection and analysis. The approach involves fine-tuning the LLMs to improve their adaptability to complex and diverse log data. Moreover, It incorporates two advanced prompt engineering techniques, ToT and Self-Refine, while also exploring the combination of existing techniques such as CoT and In-Context prompting. These three different prompt engineering methods significantly enhance the LLMs' the accuracy in log anomaly detection and the quality in generation of log anomaly analysis.
